title: A teaspoon of neutron star would weigh billions of tonnes
body: When a massive star explodes as a supernova, its core can collapse into a ball only about 20 km across that holds around 1.4 times the Sun’s mass. Gravity crushes the matter to the density of an atomic nucleus, made mostly of neutrons. A teaspoon of it would have a mass of about 5.5 billion tonnes, roughly 900 Great Pyramids. Many neutron stars also spin furiously; the fastest known turns about 716 times a second.

slides.question: How many times a second does the fastest known neutron star spin?
slides.explanation: About 716 times a second. Such a star packs around 1.4 times the Sun’s mass into a ball only about 20 km across, at the density of an atomic nucleus.
